issues: Figure 4 sequence logic bug: the NACK branch ends with 'CTL->>CS: Rollout failed, Nodes keep prior Revision', then outside the alt the flow continues unconditionally to 'CTL->>CS: Rollout progressing' and 'Rollout complete', so a failed canary still appears to progress to complete.

LKG ordering contradicts itself: Figure 4 shows 'atomic swap, persist Last-Known-Good' before 'ACK', but the Compile before swap list says step 4 'Publishes the snapshot ... then ACKs' and only step 5 'Writes the Revision to ${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/lkg/'. An implementer can't tell whether ACK means the Revision is durable.

LKG is persisted on local activation, so a canary Revision that passes compile but fails health gates becomes what a restarted Node boots. The draft never addresses this (draft 3 does, in OQ-system-overview-2).
NACK outcome is ambiguous: the failure table says 'NACK; Rollout becomes `failed` or `rolled-back`' without saying which state applies when.

Figure 1 collapses all four components into one box ('Ruralz: Ruralz Gateway, Ruralz Control, Ruralz Console, ruralz CLI'), so the context view can't show that Git feeds Ruralz Control while OCI feeds Nodes directly.
Control Stream arrows are drawn 'CTL -->|Control Stream ...| GW', which reads as Control dialing Nodes. Who dials whom is never stated, and that matters for NAT and firewalls.
Word count about 3,967 including diagrams once table pipes are stripped. It passes, but only just, so any grafts must be offset by cuts.

Internal contradiction on Git write access: 'Ruralz Console and the REST API write back to Git' and 'Ruralz Console edits become commits or pull requests against the Bundle repository', but TB-6 says 'Read-only repository credentials'.

States unsettled security design as fact with no ADR behind it: 'validate, render overlay, build and sign' and TB-5 'Nodes verify Revision signatures'. The foundation pack and ADR-0007 say nothing about signing, and the draft's own OQ-system-overview-4 covers only file mode.

Figure 4 puts the failure path after success: 'RC->>CS: Rollout complete' comes before 'alt any Node NACKs or a gate fails ... Rollout rolled-back', and the rollback reactivates only N1, not the N2 batches.

Figure 3 sends onChunk output to the client ('F-->>C: chunk') and only then runs 'onResponse', which contradicts its own table ('onResponse | The client response is assembled'). It also shows 'F->>U: forward', with the Filter Chain rather than the Upstream layer doing the forwarding.

'Clusters that render identical bytes share a Revision, which proves that `staging` and `prod` run the same configuration' contradicts its own model, where a Revision is 'the digest of the rendered Bundle for one Environment' with per-Environment overlays.

Container view has 'CSS -.-> LKG', meaning the Control Stream server writes the Node's disk directly, and uses subgraph-to-subgraph edges ('Control --> CST', 'CSS <-->|mTLS gRPC| Node') that don't show the Node-side Control Stream client or config loader.

Gives the implementer no hot-path contract: no latency, allocation or State Store round-trip budget, and no rule for which phases run after a short-circuit. The only figure is 'within 60 seconds of leaving canary (target)'.
About 4,172 words including code and diagram fences, which puts the 4,000-word acceptance criterion at risk.
Longest draft at about 4,566 words including diagrams (3,905 without code fences), so it likely fails the 'body is 4,000 words or fewer' acceptance criterion and the max_words machine check.

States Revision signing as decided with no ADR behind it: 'build and sign Revision', 'Revisions signed by Ruralz Control and verified by the Node | Unsigned or mis-signed Revisions are NACKed', 'verifies the stored digest and signature at boot', and for OCI 'signature verified before use'. The foundation pack leaves signing undecided.

Node state machine contradicts the failure table: Figure 5 has 'Serving --> ServingLKG: Control Stream lost', but the failure table says 'Keep active Revision; restart boots Last-Known-Good'. With the draft's own proposal to promote LKG only on `complete`, a canary Node that loses the stream would be serving a Revision that isn't LKG, and the draft doesn't say whether it reverts.
Figure 4 says 'Op->>G: merge change to the Environment branch', which assumes branch-per-Environment. The foundation model uses overlays under 'overlays/<env>/'.
Container view edge 'csrv -.->|snapshot and delta, ACK or NACK| lis' delivers configuration to the client Listeners instead of a config loader. 'csrv -.-> lkg' has Ruralz Control writing Node disk.

Figure 3 collapses phases into self-messages and message labels ('U-->>F: onUpstreamResponseBody, onChunk per event or token'), and swaps the 'Ruralz Gateway' participant for 'Router', so the phase boundaries are harder to implement from.
Trust diagram (Figure 6) has no admin port 9901 and no OCI-to-Node edge, though its table covers both.
The four differentiators are pushed under Document map as an H3. That's allowed, but they sit away from the Component map where readers expect them.

graft_suggestions.section: Configuration lifecycle > Node configuration states (Figure 5 stateDiagram-v2) and /readyz semantics
graft_suggestions.why: Draft 1 never defines readiness or boot behavior. Draft 3's rule ('has a validated Revision, listeners bound, not draining'; losing the Control Stream does not change readiness; a new Node with no LKG stays not ready) is directly implementable. Fix the 'Serving --> ServingLKG' transition when grafting so it says the Node keeps its active Revision.

graft_suggestions.section: Configuration lifecycle > Last-Known-Good and Hot Reload (promote LKG on Rollout complete, OQ-system-overview-2)
graft_suggestions.why: Draft 1 persists LKG on local activation, so a Revision that failed its canary gate can become the boot configuration. Draft 3 names this hazard and records it as an open question, which also resolves draft 1's ACK-versus-persist ordering ambiguity. Graft it without the signature claims.

graft_suggestions.section: Cross-cutting concerns > Failure semantics at component boundaries
graft_suggestions.why: This table is more complete than draft 1's five-row failure table. It covers the IdP/JWKS outage (cached keys, then fail closed), Plugin traps, an unwritable LKG directory, zone loss and LLM provider throttling, each with blast radius and owner. Merge it with draft 1's table in Deployment modes.

graft_suggestions.section: Request lifecycle > Worked example: State Store brownout
graft_suggestions.why: It spells out the two-level Rate Limit degradation: per-Node bound on fail-open, State Store client circuit breaker, fail-closed spend limits with RZ-STS, and fail-open counters. That complements draft 1's happy-path worked example and gives the SRE angle.

graft_suggestions.section: Component map > System context note ('Nodes always dial Ruralz Control, never the reverse') and Configuration lifecycle > Reconnect behavior
graft_suggestions.why: It fixes the connection direction, which matters for NAT and egress-only firewalls, and the reconnect storm mitigation (full jitter, resume by digest, load shedding). Draft 1's arrows leave the direction ambiguous.

graft_suggestions.section: Configuration lifecycle > Rollout state table (Meaning, Operator signal)
graft_suggestions.why: It gives each of the six states a distinct meaning, and so settles draft 1's ambiguous 'NACK; Rollout becomes failed or rolled-back'.

graft_suggestions.section: Deployment modes intro ('A Node runs in exactly one configuration mode, chosen at boot, and never merges configuration from two sources')
graft_suggestions.why: A crisp invariant that tells the config loader what it must not do. Draft 1 doesn't state it.

graft_suggestions.section: Cross-cutting concerns closing paragraph (Hot Reload vs Rollout vs Zero-Downtime Upgrade)
graft_suggestions.why: A short, precise definition of three terms that component documents will otherwise blur.

graft_suggestions.section: Configuration lifecycle > Tradeoff: why a Control Stream when OCI pull exists
graft_suggestions.why: It justifies ADR-0007 from the operator's side: per-Node ACK/NACK, convergence without tight polling, and a live Revision inventory. Draft 1's tradeoff row only compares against xDS.

graft_suggestions.section: Open questions OQ-system-overview-2 (CRD vs Git source of desired state), -3 (canary gate signal source), -5 (may onRoute re-match)
graft_suggestions.why: These are real unresolved design forks that block M2 Kubernetes packaging, Rollouts and the data-plane router. Draft 1's open questions miss them.

issues: Figure 4 (Configuration lifecycle) has a broken flow. After the failure branch `CTL->>CS: Rollout failed, Nodes keep prior Revision`, the `end` falls through to `CTL->>CS: Rollout progressing` and `Rollout complete`, so the diagram shows a failed canary going on to finish the Rollout.

The NACK outcome contradicts itself. The diagram says `Rollout failed`, but the Deployment modes failure table says "NACK; Rollout becomes `failed` or `rolled-back`". An operator cannot tell which terminal state a canary NACK produces.

Last-Known-Good is written on every activation ("5. Writes the Revision to `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/lkg/` as Last-Known-Good"). A Revision that compiles but fails canary health therefore becomes the boot config after a restart. Nothing says whether `/readyz` changes when the Control Stream is lost.

Figure 2 draws `CTL -->|"Control Stream, gRPC over mTLS"| GW`, which suggests Ruralz Control dials the Nodes. The document never says which side opens the connection, which matters for NAT and egress-only firewalls.

The overview restates a full budget table that doc 12 owns ("Gateway-added latency, p50 ... 150 µs or less (target)"). It also includes "Requests reaching the State Store under steady load | 10% or less with local buckets (hypothesis)" without saying how a local bucket knows when it "cannot decide", so the claim cannot be checked against GCRA global accuracy.
It leaves almost no length headroom: 3,974 words by plain whitespace count against the 4,000 cap (3,422 with table pipes excluded).

Figure 4 puts `alt any Node NACKs or a gate fails` after `RC->>CS: Rollout complete`, which shows a rollback after completion. The rollback branch also only does `RC->>N1: reactivate previous Revision`.

Figure 3 calls the State Store unconditionally (`F->>S: GCRA check after local token bucket` / `S-->>F: allow`). That implies every request pays a State Store round trip, which contradicts the local-first intent of ADR-0008.

There is no failure matrix. State Store outage is covered only by "fail mode declared per Policy", and there are no readiness or reconnect-storm semantics. The only performance figure is a 60 s convergence target, so a platform lead cannot judge whether the hot path is feasible.

Three ADR citations point at the wrong ADR: the Performance row cites [ADR-0009] (the HTTP stack ADR); "Build and supply chain ... signed Revisions" cites [ADR-0001] (the language ADR); Migration `ruralz bundle import krakend` cites ADR-0003.
The Bundle anatomy block invents a directory convention (`routes/10-orders.yaml`, `upstreams/`, `policies/`) that the Configuration Model owns.
"A Revision is the digest of the rendered Bundle for one Environment" goes beyond the foundation definition ("content-addressed digest of a Bundle") without proposing a foundation amendment.
Figure 2 has `CSS -.-> LKG`, meaning the Control Stream server writes the Node's disk. Last-Known-Good is persisted by the Node.

Length risk. It is the longest draft: 4,377 words by plain whitespace count (3,870 with table pipes excluded) against max_words 4000 and the acceptance criterion "The body is 4,000 words or fewer". Whether it passes depends on how the counter treats pipes, and any graft pushes it over.

Figure 4 opens with `Op->>G: merge change to the Environment branch`, which assumes one branch per Environment. The foundation's overlay model is `overlays/<env>/`, and no open question covers the branch-to-Environment mapping.

Figure 2 draws `csrv -.->|"snapshot and delta, ACK or NACK"| lis`: the Control Stream goes into the Listeners instead of a config loader. It also has `csrv -.-> lkg`, meaning Ruralz Control writes the Node's disk.

It states commitments with no source: "Ruralz Control and Nodes tolerate version skew of N and N-1" and "Planned (M0) for `ruralz bundle validate`". It also misuses `(target)` on a topology choice: "3 or 5 Raft voters (target)".

The Trust boundaries table says "OCI registry and Git ... Pinned by digest; signature verified before use", but never says who signs a Revision in file mode, where there is no Ruralz Control. Draft 2 raises this correctly as an open question.

Figure 4 models a NACK only from canary Nodes; there is no NACK path from Remaining Nodes during `progressing`. `CT-->>N1: promote Revision to Last-Known-Good` adds a new Control Stream message semantic before OQ-system-overview-2 is decided.
"HTTP/3 terminates in `quic-go` on UDP 8443" has no milestone tag and no open question, while drafts 1 and 2 both track the HTTP/3 milestone as OQ-1.

graft_suggestions.why: Draft 1's 'Tradeoffs these rules accept' table gives each fixed technology choice (net/http without fasthttp, wazero and Plugin ABI v1, external State Store with no gossip, whole-snapshot swap, own Control Stream instead of xDS) with its cost, rationale and recovery. Draft 3 covers only the availability-versus-freshness tradeoff. To pay for it, replace Draft 3's 'Binaries are boring' row and trim the Scope prose so the body stays under 4,000 words.

Draft 1's 'Compile before swap' numbered steps are the concrete Node-side activation contract missing from Draft 3's one-sentence Hot Reload description: verify digest, build router and chains, compile CEL and Plugins ahead of time with digest reuse, pre-warm pools, atomic publish, ACK, free the old snapshot. Draft 1's 'reconnect with jittered backoff and resume from their Revision digest' is already covered by Draft 3.

Draft 1's 'Inside a Node' table (Listeners, Router, Filter Chain executor, Plugin host, Upstream manager, State client, Config loader, Admin) gives each part a hot-path rule. It also fixes Draft 3's Figure 2 edge by giving the Control Stream a named Config loader target instead of the Listeners.

Draft 2's 'Tradeoff: why a Control Stream when OCI pull exists' is the strongest justification any draft gives for adopting Control mode: per-Node ACK/NACK, convergence without tight polling, and a live Revision inventory. Draft 2's OQ on default branch-to-Environment mapping should also replace Draft 3's hardcoded 'merge change to the Environment branch' in Figure 4.

Draft 2's TB-1 to TB-8 IDs make the boundaries citable from Security and Identity. Its OQ-system-overview-4 (how file-mode Nodes verify Revision and Plugin signatures without Ruralz Control) closes the gap left by Draft 3's unqualified 'signature verified before use'.

Draft 2's 'Choosing a mode' paragraph and its CRD source-of-truth open question (OQ-system-overview-2: Git Bundles versus CRDs) give a platform lead a clear adoption path and flag a real Planned (M2) Kubernetes conflict that Draft 3 does not mention.

issues: Figure 4 (Configuration lifecycle): after the `alt compile fails` branch ends with 'CTL->>CS: Rollout failed, Nodes keep prior Revision', the diagram carries on outside the alt with 'CTL->>CS: Rollout progressing' and 'CTL->>N2: Control Stream delta in batches'. As drawn, a failed canary still progresses to the remaining Nodes. The success path should sit inside an else branch.
Figure 4 records a canary NACK as `failed`, but the failure table says 'NACK; Rollout becomes `failed` or `rolled-back`'. The document never says which state a canary NACK produces.

Last-Known-Good is written on activation: 'Publishes the snapshot ... then ACKs', then 'Writes the Revision to `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/lkg/` as Last-Known-Good'. So a Revision that later fails the canary becomes the boot configuration after a restart. This hazard is neither addressed nor raised as an open question (draft 3 catches it).
Scope and non-goals contains the literal 'Every capability carries a `Planned (Mx)` tag.' 'Mx' is not M0..M5 and may trip a milestone-tag check (it is in code formatting, which lowers the risk).
Figure 3 has no short-circuit path, even though the prose says 'A short-circuit skips the remaining request and upstream phases, then runs `onResponse` and `onLog`'.
Deployment modes asserts 'One `redis` State Store handles 100,000 GCRA operations per second before sharding is needed (hypothesis)'. The tag makes it compliant, but nothing grounds the number.
The failure table covers only 5 failure modes. There is no readiness semantics (/readyz during a Control outage) and nothing on a reconnect storm after a Ruralz Control failover.

Revision signing is presented as settled fact, although the foundation pack never mentions it. Configuration lifecycle says 'Ruralz Control ingests the merged commit, validates, renders and signs it'. TB-5 says 'Nodes verify Revision signatures'. Cross-cutting says 'signed Revisions'. Only file-mode verification is raised as OQ-system-overview-4.

A Git write-back model is made a design principle without an ADR or open question: 'Ruralz Console and the REST API write back to Git' and 'Git stays the only writer of desired state'. It then conflicts with OQ-system-overview-7 (break-glass Bundle applied to a Node).
Figure 2 (container view) draws 'CSS -.-> LKG': the Control Stream server writing Last-Known-Good on the Node's disk. The Node persists Last-Known-Good, not Ruralz Control.
Figure 4 puts 'alt any Node NACKs or a gate fails ... Rollout rolled-back' after 'RC->>CS: Rollout complete', so the diagram shows a rollback after completion.

The Cross-cutting concerns ADR column mismatches ADRs to concerns: Performance -> ADR-0009 (HTTP stack), Traffic resilience -> ADR-0008 (rate limiting only), Migration -> ADR-0003 (config format) for `ruralz bundle import krakend`.

'Last-Known-Good is Planned (M2)' sits next to 'File mode ... Planned (M1) directory watch', whose deployment-table Last-Known-Good cell reads 'Current snapshot'. The acceptance-critical Last-Known-Good behavior is thin for the M1 file mode.
'A Revision is the digest of the rendered Bundle for one Environment' refines the foundation's 'content-addressed digest of a Bundle' without raising it for foundation_amendments.

The data plane is thin: no hot-path contract, no Performance Budget figures beyond the '60 seconds' Rollout convergence target, and no failure matrix. The SRE and performance panel angles go largely unaddressed.

Revision signing is presented as fact, although the foundation pack is silent on it: 'CT->>CT: validate Bundle, build and sign Revision', 'verifies the stored digest and signature at boot', trust table 'Revisions signed by Ruralz Control and verified by the Node' and 'signature verified before use'. It should be an open question or a foundation amendment.

Figure 4 says 'Op->>G: merge change to the Environment branch', which assumes branch-per-Environment. The foundation pack fixes overlays under `overlays/<env>/`, and no open question covers the branch mapping.

Figure 2 edges are wrong. 'csrv -.->|"snapshot and delta, ACK or NACK"| lis' ends the Control Stream at the Listeners instead of a config loader, and 'csrv -.-> lkg' shows Ruralz Control writing the Node's Last-Known-Good.
Summary says 'every capability is tagged Planned (Mx)' in plain prose. 'Mx' is not a valid M0..M5 tag and is likely to trip the milestone-tag check.

Milestone and compatibility commitments are invented without anchors: '`ruralz` CLI ... Planned (M0) for `ruralz bundle validate`' and 'Ruralz Control and Nodes tolerate version skew of N and N-1'. Both belong to the roadmap and release documents.
'(target)' is misused on a non-performance count: '`ruralz-control` with 3 or 5 Raft voters (target)'.
The Filter Chain phases are given as a comma list rather than the foundation's verbatim arrow form. This is acceptable, but drafts 1 and 2 reproduce it exactly.
It discusses SO_REUSEPORT upgrades and the Helm chart and CRDs but links neither ADR-0015 nor ADR-0016.
The body is roughly 3,870 words by my count, the closest of the three to the 4,000-word cap, so later revisions have little room.

graft_suggestions.why: The 'Failure semantics at component boundaries' table has 11 rows, with blast radius, Node behavior, what stops and owner. It covers IdP/JWKS loss, Plugin trap, an unwritable Last-Known-Good directory and zone loss. It is much stronger than draft 1's 5-row failure table and serves the SRE panel angle. Drop draft 3's signing assumptions when grafting.

The 'Node configuration states' stateDiagram-v2 and its readiness semantics fill a gap in draft 1: losing the Control Stream does not fail /readyz, and a new Node with no Last-Known-Good stays not ready. So do 'Reconnect behavior' (jittered reconnect carrying the last-ACKed digest, with load shedding) and the Last-Known-Good-promotion-on-complete proposal (OQ-system-overview-2). The last one fixes draft 1's hidden hazard of booting a canary-failed Revision.

The 'State Store brownout' worked example makes the local bucket plus GCRA fail-open tradeoff concrete, with bounded over-admission and explicit fail-closed Quotas via RZ-STS. Draft 3's Figure 3 also draws the short-circuit branch, which draft 1's Figure 3 omits.

The transposed comparison table, with modes as columns and rows for source, components, Rollout mechanism and Last-Known-Good, plus the 'Choosing a mode' guidance ('No step rewrites configuration or changes the binary'), reads more clearly for evaluators than draft 1's single table.

'Tradeoff: why a Control Stream when OCI pull exists' gives the best justification of ADR-0007 in any draft. The one-line definitions of all six Rollout states and 'Promotion across Environments' also add GitOps substance draft 1 lacks. Graft them without the Git write-back and signing claims, or move those claims to Open questions.
TB-1..TB-8 IDs appear on both the diagram edges and the table rows, which ties Figure 5 to the table better than draft 1's unlabeled edges.

foundation_amendments: Section 2, Control Stream row: state that Nodes always dial `ruralz-control` on 8091 and Revisions flow down that Node-initiated stream, because connection direction decides NAT and egress-only firewall compatibility and the three drafts disagreed on it.

Section 2, Last-Known-Good row: add the promotion rule that a Revision becomes Last-Known-Good when its Rollout reaches `complete` in Control mode and on activation in file mode, because promoting on activation lets a Revision that failed its canary gate become the boot configuration after a restart (OQ-system-overview-2).

Section 2, Rollout row: give each state a one-line meaning, in particular that any NACK or failed gate ends in `rolled-back` and `failed` means only that the revert itself could not finish, because the drafts assigned a canary NACK to different terminal states.

Section 7: add a row, backed by a new ADR, deciding whether Revisions and Plugin artifacts are signed, who signs them in file mode and Control mode, and whether Nodes verify by default, because every draft asserted or assumed signing that the foundation pack never decides (OQ-system-overview-3).

Section 2, Default ports row: add a default Raft peer port for `ruralz-control`, or state that Raft traffic is multiplexed over 8091, because the embedded Control Store needs peer traffic and the pack lists only 8090 and 8091 (OQ-system-overview-7).

Section 2, Revision row: say whether the digest covers the Bundle source or the Bundle rendered with one Environment overlay, because that decides whether Environments can share a Revision and what Drift detection compares (OQ-system-overview-14).
Section 7, ADR-0009 row: assign HTTP/3 on UDP 8443 a milestone tag, because the ports row reserves UDP 8443 but no milestone is given and component documents need one (OQ-system-overview-1).

Section 2, Default ports row: state that `/readyz` reports an active validated Revision, bound listeners and no drain, and does not fail when the Control Stream is lost, because failing readiness during a control-plane outage would pull every Node from load balancing at once.
